prompt: Modernize flow's supervisor architecture around 2026 Claude Code harness primitives, based on the completed research review (pipeline review-research-related-even-newer, phase triaged-no-change). Keep the confirmed-right architecture (discovery → coder → multi-lens review split, .flow-tmp artifacts + state.json + checkpoint/clear, the UI-smoke active-evaluator pass, plan Contract blocks + the Test Steps auto-merge rubric) and flow's differentiators (auto-merge gate rubric, cross-model review, resource-teardown discipline). Address the outdated compensations: the hand-rolled prose state machine, the nine-exemption ledger's outlived platform rationale, tmux-derived identity plumbing, flow-ci-wait's owned poll loop (the false-ci-hang bug class), and 200k-era context-isolation scaffolds — measurement first, one measured removal at a time, with re-verified platform claims recorded in design.md.

features.title: Flow-owned eval harness + baseline scaffold suites
features.description: Build a flow-owned, locally-runnable eval harness that makes supervisor-scaffold removals measurable: a bin/flow-eval runner (Bun, maintainer-run) that executes small fixed headless scenario suites and scores them with deterministic graders over the artifacts flow already emits (state.json fields, .flow-tmp/*-result.json shapes, transcript-derived signals), emitting a machine-readable JSON report plus a human summary. Do NOT anchor on `claude plugin eval` — it is org-gated early access (verified 2026-08-19) and flow's CI installs no claude binary; instead mirror flow-plugin-contract-lint's pattern (local signal, named skip with notice when claude is absent, vitest stays the CI gate) and keep the report schema as a stable seam so `claude plugin eval` can become a runner backend once GA. Ship committed baseline suites for the three stress-test candidates — verify-loop subagent isolation, the haiku gatekeeper, checkpoint-pending-clear — and record their baseline scores. Part of epic `modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture` (feature `f1-eval-harness`) — design at `.flow/epics/modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D1 (how supervisor behavior is scored) behind a stable flow-eval CLI + report schema; the walking-skeleton root the measured-removal bet hangs off.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a maintainer runs the flow-eval runner on a named suite THE SYSTEM SHALL execute its scenarios and emit a machine-readable JSON score report plus a human-readable summary
WHEN the runner is invoked where no claude binary is available (e.g. CI) THE SYSTEM SHALL skip with a named notice and exit 0, leaving vitest as the CI gate
WHEN the three candidate baseline suites are run on an unchanged tree THE SYSTEM SHALL produce recorded baseline scores from deterministic artifact graders, not free-form LLM judgment alone

features.title: Eval-gated stress-test of the three 200k-era scaffolds
features.description: Behind the f1-eval-harness suites, stress-test the three context-isolation scaffolds sized for 200k-token windows (current models carry 1M windows — verified 2026-08-19), one candidate at a time: the verify-loop subagent isolation, the haiku gatekeeper, and checkpoint-pending-clear. For each candidate: remove it on its own commit, run the f1 suite before/after, and either keep the removal (delta clean) or revert and record a keep-verdict with the measured evidence — never a silent retention. Treat checkpoint-pending-clear as keep-biased: its eval must specifically cover the post-/clear resume path (PR #640's orientation turn touches the same machinery). Land a committed keep/remove verdict table (consumed by the workflow-port feature) and correct the stale nested-subagent depth-cap citation in docs/nested-subagents-assessment.md (default cap is now 3, env-overridable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH — not 5). Part of epic `modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture` (feature `f2-scaffold-stress-test`) — design at `.flow/epics/modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D2 (which scaffolds survive — a measurement outcome, not an architecture commitment) behind the committed verdict table + eval suites.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a candidate scaffold is removed THE SYSTEM SHALL carry a before/after eval delta for that candidate, one candidate per commit
WHEN a candidate's delta shows regression THE SYSTEM SHALL retain the scaffold and record a keep-verdict with the measured evidence in the committed verdict table
WHEN all three candidates are adjudicated THE SYSTEM SHALL have committed a verdict table naming each candidate's outcome and evidence
WHEN docs/nested-subagents-assessment.md cites the nesting depth cap THE SYSTEM SHALL state the current contract (default 3, env-overridable), not the stale 5

features.title: Split flow-ci-wait into a harness-native wait + one-shot flow-ci-check
features.description: Retire flow-ci-wait's hand-rolled 20-minute poll loop (bin/flow-ci-wait.ts, ~1,851 lines — the source of the false-ci-hang bug class where a suspended background process inflates its in-process elapsed clock) by separating waiting from deciding. Deciding: extract a one-shot deterministic flow-ci-check helper that computes the existing CI/Copilot decision matrix (decideOnPoll, deriveCheckState, deriveCopilotSkipReason and friends — moved with their unit tests, not rewritten) from a single fresh GitHub observation plus wall-clock anchor timestamps persisted in ~/.flow/state/<slug>.json, so elapsed time derives from durable timestamps and a suspended or slept process can never fabricate ci-hang. Waiting: a dumb, restartable, policy-free waiter driven by harness-native primitives — a backgrounded blocking wait whose exit wakes the session via the completion notification, with Monitor/ScheduleWakeup (60s floor supersedes the 30s early cadence) as the cadence fallback — per the verified 2026-08-19 background-task semantics (completion notification + transcript capture; processes resume across machine sleep). Update skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/references/polling-protocol.md and the step-7 runbook accordingly, and add a suspension-immunity regression test. Part of epic `modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture` (feature `f3-ci-check-split`) — design at `.flow/epics/modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D3 (how waiting happens — a swappable harness primitive) behind the stable, unit-tested verdict matrix now exposed as one-shot flow-ci-check.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN the supervisor reaches the CI wait THE SYSTEM SHALL wait via harness-native primitives (background completion notification, Monitor/ScheduleWakeup) instead of a helper-owned verdict loop
WHEN the session wakes THE SYSTEM SHALL compute the verdict via one-shot flow-ci-check from live GitHub state plus timestamps persisted in state.json
WHEN the waiter process is suspended, slept, or killed THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT emit ci-hang from inflated in-process elapsed time — a regression test covers the suspension scenario
WHEN the split lands THE SYSTEM SHALL preserve the existing decision-matrix functions and their unit tests (moved, not rewritten) and the CI/Copilot decision taxonomy unchanged

features.title: Finish env/state-only session identity
features.description: Complete the env/state-only session-identity migration: audit every tmux pane-option read site (the @flow-slug/@flow-phase/@flow-repo/@flow-phase-short/@flow-kind consumers across bin/*.ts, bin/lib/*, and the pipeline skills' prose) and drop pane-option READS everywhere except the epic-orchestration surfaces that are tmux-only by independent hard constraint — resolveKindAmbient's documented contract in bin/lib/session-identity.ts, with its bidirectional producing/consuming-site comments kept intact. Identity resolves from FLOW_SLUG (launch env, both backends) then ~/.flow/state/<slug>.json then on-disk artifacts, per AGENTS.md's backend-agnostic signal order; tmux options remain additive publish-only mirrors, and any option nothing consumes anymore is deleted rather than left as cargo. Add a structural lint (test-enforced grep, mirroring skill-md-lint's pattern) pinning that no pane-option read exists outside tmux.ts and the named epic surfaces, and verify the plain-shell launcher path end-to-end (env -u FLOW_SLUG test suite stays green). Part of epic `modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture` (feature `f4-env-state-identity`) — design at `.flow/epics/modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides D4 (the identity carrier) behind session-identity.ts once and for all; plain shell is the default launcher, so pane-derived identity is legacy plumbing.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN any helper or skill resolves pipeline identity outside the documented tmux-only epic surfaces THE SYSTEM SHALL read FLOW_SLUG/state.json, never a tmux pane option
WHEN running under the tmux launcher THE SYSTEM SHALL keep pane options as additive publish-only mirrors, with unconsumed options deleted
WHEN a pane-option read is introduced outside tmux.ts or the named epic surfaces THE SYSTEM SHALL fail a structural lint test
WHEN the epic-orchestration surfaces read @flow-kind THE SYSTEM SHALL retain the documented tmux-only exception with safe-by-construction absence defaults

features.title: Throwaway workflow spike + go/no-go ADR for the steps-5-10 port
features.description: Run a throwaway spike against the Claude Code dynamic-workflow runtime (verified GA 2026-08-19 at code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows.md, but with flow-critical capabilities undocumented) and commit a go/no-go ADR for porting pipeline steps 5-10. The spike must exercise, live, the four load-bearing capabilities the port depends on: (1) invoking flow's PATH-bound Bash helpers from workflow steps, (2) spawning flow's named agents by plugin-qualified name (flow-module-core:flow-scout etc.) with their frontmatter model/effort pins honored, (3) handing control back to the supervisor session at a human gate (the workflow must be able to STOP at gate verdicts, not merge), and (4) resume semantics after interruption, reconciled against ~/.flow/state/<slug>.json as the durable anchor. Record per-capability evidence (confirmed/refuted, with the observed behavior) in a committed ADR mirroring the p6-distribution-eval precedent, ending in a go/no-go verdict plus the fallback (retain the prose state machine) on no-go. Nothing from the spike ships to consumers; the spike script is committed as evidence only. Part of epic `modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture` (feature `f5-workflow-spike`) — design at `.flow/epics/modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides the evidence half of D5 (does the workflow runtime actually support flow's four load-bearing capabilities) so the port never designs on undocumented claims.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN the spike completes THE SYSTEM SHALL have committed an ADR with a go/no-go verdict backed by live per-capability evidence for all four named capabilities
WHEN any capability is refuted THE SYSTEM SHALL name the refuted capability and the fallback rung in the ADR rather than asserting the port is viable
WHEN the spike lands THE SYSTEM SHALL ship nothing to consumer-facing surfaces (no skill, helper, or install change beyond the committed ADR and spike script)

features.title: Port pipeline steps 5-10 to a deterministic workflow script
features.description: CONTINGENT feature — proceed only if f5-workflow-spike's ADR records go AND f2-scaffold-stress-test's verdicts leave the port's premise intact; on a no-go, cancel this feature at the epic-run checkpoint and record why (the prose state machine is retained for steps 5-10). Port the mechanical middle of /flow-pipeline (steps 5-10: implement, verify, ci-wait, review, gate mechanics, merge mechanics) from the prose state machine in skills/pipeline/flow-pipeline/SKILL.md (~2,733 lines) to a committed deterministic workflow script, keeping the LLM supervisor session for the human-in-the-loop phases (triage, plan review, and the gate verdict — the workflow stops at gate and hands back; the auto-merge exemption's fresh-confirmation contract is preserved byte-equivalent in behavior, as are the auto-merge rubric, cross-model review, and resource-teardown discipline). The ported step 7 invokes f3's one-shot flow-ci-check; the ported steps carry only the scaffolds f2's verdict table kept. Dissolve the Task-tool exemption prose for the ported spawn sites into workflow code (the exemption ledger shrinks to the sites that remain supervisor-driven), slim SKILL.md accordingly, and gate the port on the f1/f2 eval suites showing no regression against the prose baseline. Part of epic `modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture` (feature `f6-workflow-port`) — design at `.flow/epics/modernize-flow-s-supervisor-architecture/design.md`.
features.rationale: Hides the commitment half of D5 (the orchestration substrate for the mechanical middle) behind the workflow script, consuming the spike ADR, the scaffold verdicts, and the ci-check helper.
acceptanceCriteria: WHEN a feature pipeline reaches step 5 with the port landed THE SYSTEM SHALL drive steps 5-10 via the committed workflow script while triage, plan review, and the gate verdict remain supervisor turns
WHEN the workflow reaches the gate THE SYSTEM SHALL stop and hand back to the supervisor — a gated verdict is never merged by the workflow, preserving the fresh-confirmation gate-override contract
WHEN the workflow run is interrupted THE SYSTEM SHALL resume without losing pipeline state, with state.json remaining the durable anchor
WHEN the port lands THE SYSTEM SHALL pass the f1/f2 eval suites with no regression against the prose baseline, and the ported sites' Task-tool exemption prose SHALL be dissolved into workflow code
